sanskrit: raṇe tavārthāya mahānubhāva; na jīvitaṃ rakṣyatamaṃ mamādya sarvāṃs tavārthāya sadevadaityāṃl; lokān daheyaṃ kim u śatrūṃs taveha
english: In battle, for your sake, O mighty one, my life is no longer the thing I will most guard this day. For your sake I would burn up all the worlds, gods and demons alike — how much more, then, your enemies here.

sanskrit: tat pāṇḍavān yodhayiṣyāmi rājan; priyaṃ ca te sarvam ahaṃ kariṣye śrutvaiva caitat paramapratīto; duryodhanaḥ prītamanā babhūva
english: Therefore I will do battle with the Pāṇḍavas, O king, and I will do all that is dear to you." Hearing this very thing, Duryodhana grew supremely confident and glad of heart.

sanskrit: sarvāṇi sainyāni tataḥ prahṛṣṭo; nirgacchatety āha nṛpāṃś ca sarvān tadājñayā tāni viniryayur drutaṃ; rathāśvapādātagajāyutāni
english: Then, full of joy, he commanded all the armies and all the kings: "March forth!" At his order they swiftly issued out — myriads of chariots, horses, foot-soldiers, and elephants.

sanskrit: praharṣayuktāni tu tāni rājan; mahānti nānāvidhaśastravanti sthitāni nāgāśvapadātimanti; virejur ājau tava rājan balāni
english: Filled with high spirit, O king, vast, bristling with weapons of every kind, arrayed with elephants and horses and foot-soldiers, your forces shone resplendent upon the field of battle, O king.

sanskrit: vṛndaiḥ sthitāś cāpi susaṃprayuktāś; cakāśire dantigaṇāḥ samantāt śastrāstravidbhir naradeva yodhair; adhiṣṭhitāḥ sainyagaṇās tvadīyāḥ
english: Drawn up in well-marshalled bands, the herds of tusked elephants blazed forth on every side; and your troops, O lord of men, were commanded by warriors skilled in weapons and missiles.

sanskrit: rathaiś ca pādātagajāśvasaṃghaiḥ; prayādbhir ājau vidhivat praṇunnaiḥ samuddhataṃ vai taruṇārkavarṇaṃ; rajo babhau chādayat sūryaraśmīn
english: By the chariots and the massed foot-soldiers, elephants, and horses, advancing into battle in proper order as they were urged on, dust of the hue of the newly risen sun was raised up, and it shone as it veiled the very rays of the sun.

sanskrit: rejuḥ patākā rathadantisaṃsthā; vāteritā bhrāmyamāṇāḥ samantāt nānāraṅgāḥ samare tatra rājan; meghair yuktā vidyutaḥ khe yathaiva
english: The banners set upon chariots and elephants, stirred by the wind and whirling on every side, shone in that battle, O king — of many colors, like flashes of lightning ranged with clouds in the sky.

sanskrit: dhanūṃṣi visphārayatāṃ nṛpāṇāṃ; babhūva śabdas tumulo 'tighoraḥ vimathyato devamahāsuraughair; yathārṇavasyādiyuge tadānīm
english: As the kings twanged their bows, there arose a tumultuous and terrible din, like that of the ocean churned by the hosts of gods and great demons in the first age of the world.

sanskrit: tad ugranādaṃ bahurūpavarṇaṃ; tavātmajānāṃ samudīrṇam evam babhūva sainyaṃ ripusainyahantṛ; yugāntameghaughanibhaṃ tadānīm
english: Roaring fiercely, of many forms and colors, the army of your sons surged up in this manner — destroyer of the enemy's host, resembling the massed clouds at the ending of an age.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca athātmajaṃ tava punar gāṅgeyo dhyānam āsthitam abravīd bharataśreṣṭhaḥ saṃpraharṣakaraṃ vacaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then to your son, who had sunk again into brooding thought, the son of Gaṅgā, foremost of the Bharatas, spoke words meant to gladden his heart.

sanskrit: ahaṃ droṇaś ca śalyaś ca kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ aśvatthāmā vikarṇaś ca somadatto 'tha saindhavaḥ
english: "I, and Droṇa, and Śalya, and Kṛtavarman of the Sātvatas, and Aśvatthāman, and Vikarṇa, and Somadatta, and the lord of the Sindhu,

sanskrit: vindānuvindāv āvantyau bāhlikaḥ saha bāhlikaiḥ trigartarājaś ca balī māgadhaś ca sudurjayaḥ
english: Vinda and Anuvinda of Avantī, Bāhlika together with the Bāhlīkas, the mighty king of the Trigartas, and the king of Magadha hard to conquer,

sanskrit: bṛhadbalaś ca kausalyaś citraseno viviṃśatiḥ rathāś ca bahusāhasrāḥ śobhamānā mahādhvajāḥ
english: and Bṛhadbala of Kosala, Citrasena, Viviṃśati, and chariot-warriors by the many thousands, splendid under their great banners —

sanskrit: deśajāś ca hayā rājan svārūḍhā hayasādibhiḥ gajendrāś ca madodvṛttāḥ prabhinnakaraṭāmukhāḥ
english: and horses of the finest breeds, O king, well mounted by their riders, and lordly elephants frenzied with rut, their cheeks and faces streaming with ichor,

sanskrit: padātāś ca tathā śūrā nānāpraharaṇāyudhāḥ nānādeśasamutpannās tvadarthe yoddhum udyatāḥ
english: and valiant foot-soldiers too, bearing weapons of every sort, sprung from many lands, are ready to fight for your sake.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavas tvadarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ devān api raṇe jetuṃ samarthā iti me matiḥ
english: These and many others, who for your sake have given up their lives, are able even to conquer the gods in battle — such is my judgment.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ tu mayā rājaṃs tava vācyaṃ hitaṃ sadā aśakyāḥ pāṇḍavā jetuṃ devair api savāsavaiḥ vāsudevasahāyāś ca mahendrasamavikramāḥ
english: Yet I must always speak to you, O king, what is for your good: the Pāṇḍavas cannot be conquered even by the gods with Vāsava at their head, for they have Vāsudeva as their ally and possess valor equal to great Indra's.

sanskrit: sarvathāhaṃ tu rājendra kariṣye vacanaṃ tava pāṇḍavān vā raṇe jeṣye māṃ vā jeṣyanti pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Nevertheless, O lord of kings, in every way I shall carry out your word: either I will conquer the Pāṇḍavas in battle, or the Pāṇḍavas will conquer me."

sanskrit: evam uktvā dadau cāsmai viśalyakaraṇīṃ śubhām oṣadhīṃ vīryasaṃpannāṃ viśalyaś cābhavat tadā
english: Having spoken thus, he gave him an auspicious herb endowed with potency, one that draws out embedded darts; and at once his wounds were freed of their shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhāte vimale svenānīkena vīryavān avyūhata svayaṃ vyūhaṃ bhīṣmo vyūhaviśāradaḥ
english: Then, when the dawn broke clear, the valiant Bhīṣma, skilled in battle-arrays, himself marshalled a formation with his own army.

sanskrit: maṇḍalaṃ manujaśreṣṭha nānāśastrasamākulam saṃpūrṇaṃ yodhamukhyaiś ca tathā dantipadātibhiḥ
english: It was the Circle array, O best of men, thick with weapons of every kind, filled with chief warriors and with elephants and foot-soldiers.

sanskrit: rathair anekasāhasraiḥ samantāt parivāritam aśvavṛndair mahadbhiś ca ṛṣṭitomaradhāribhiḥ
english: It was encircled on every side by chariots in their many thousands and by great troops of horsemen bearing swords and lances.

sanskrit: nāge nāge rathāḥ sapta sapta cāśvā rathe rathe anv aśvaṃ daśa dhānuṣkā dhānuṣke sapta carmiṇaḥ
english: To each elephant were assigned seven chariots, to each chariot seven horsemen; behind each horseman ten archers, and to each archer seven shield-bearers.

sanskrit: evaṃvyūhaṃ mahārāja tava sainyaṃ mahārathaiḥ sthitaṃ raṇāya mahate bhīṣmeṇa yudhi pālitam
english: Arrayed in this manner, O great king, with its mighty chariot-warriors, your army stood ready for the great battle, guarded in the fight by Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: daśāśvānāṃ sahasrāṇi dantināṃ ca tathaiva ca rathānām ayutaṃ cāpi putrāś ca tava daṃśitāḥ citrasenādayaḥ śūrā abhyarakṣan pitāmaham
english: Ten thousand horses, and likewise as many elephants, and ten thousand chariots besides — and your sons, clad in mail, the valiant ones led by Citrasena, guarded their grandsire on every side.

sanskrit: rakṣyamāṇaś ca taiḥ śūrair gopyamānāś ca tena te saṃnaddhāḥ samadṛśyanta rājānaś ca mahābalāḥ
english: Guarded by those heroes, and themselves shielding him in turn, the mighty kings, fully armed, were seen ranged about him.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu samare daṃśito ratham āsthitaḥ vyabhrājata śriyā juṣṭo yathā śakras triviṣṭape
english: Duryodhana, clad in armor and mounted upon his chariot in the battle, blazed forth, graced with splendor, like Śakra in the third heaven.

sanskrit: tataḥ śabdo mahān āsīt putrāṇāṃ tava bhārata rathaghoṣaś ca tumulo vāditrāṇāṃ ca nisvanaḥ
english: Then there arose a mighty clamor from your sons, O Bhārata, and the tumultuous rumble of chariots and the blare of musical instruments.

sanskrit: bhīṣmeṇa dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ vyūḍhaḥ pratyaṅmukho yudhi maṇḍalaḥ sumahāvyūho durbhedyo 'mitraghātinām sarvataḥ śuśubhe rājan raṇe 'rīṇāṃ durāsadaḥ
english: Marshalled by Bhīṣma for the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, facing westward in the fight, the Circle — a vast and mighty array, impenetrable to the slayers of foes — shone on every side, O king, hard for the enemy to approach in battle.

sanskrit: maṇḍalaṃ tu samālokya vyūhaṃ paramadāruṇam svayaṃ yudhiṣṭhiro rājā vyūhaṃ vajram athākarot
english: But beholding the Circle, that most terrible array, King Yudhiṣṭhira himself then formed the Thunderbolt array in answer.

sanskrit: tathā vyūḍheṣv anīkeṣu yathāsthānam avasthitāḥ rathinaḥ sādinaś caiva siṃhanādam athānadan
english: When the troops were thus drawn up, each stationed in his appointed place, the chariot-warriors and the horsemen raised a lion-roar.

sanskrit: bibhitsavas tato vyūhaṃ niryayur yuddhakāṅkṣiṇaḥ itaretarataḥ śūrāḥ sahasainyāḥ prahāriṇaḥ
english: Eager to break the array, longing for battle, the heroes sallied forth against one another with their troops, ready to strike.

sanskrit: bhāradvājo yayau matsyaṃ drauṇiś cāpi śikhaṇḍinam svayaṃ duryodhano rājā pārṣataṃ samupādravat
english: The son of Bharadvāja advanced upon the Matsya king, and the son of Droṇa upon Śikhaṇḍin; King Duryodhana himself rushed against the grandson of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca rājan madreśam īyatuḥ vindānuvindāv āvantyāv irāvantam abhidrutau
english: Nakula and Sahadeva, O king, went against the lord of the Madras; Vinda and Anuvinda of Avantī fell upon Irāvat.

sanskrit: sarve nṛpās tu samare dhanaṃjayam ayodhayan bhīmaseno raṇe yatto hārdikyaṃ samavārayat
english: All the kings together did battle with Dhanaṃjaya in the fight, while Bhīmasena, intent in the fray, held back the son of Hṛdika.

sanskrit: citrasenaṃ vikarṇaṃ ca tathā durmarṣaṇaṃ vibho ārjuniḥ samare rājaṃs tava putrān ayodhayat
english: Citrasena and Vikarṇa, and Durmarṣaṇa too, O lord — the son of Arjuna, O king, fought with these sons of yours in the battle.

sanskrit: prāgjyotiṣaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ haiḍimbo rākṣasottamaḥ abhidudrāva vegena matto mattam iva dvipam
english: The son of Hiḍimbā, foremost of the Rākṣasas, rushed with fury upon the great archer of Prāgjyotiṣa, as one frenzied elephant charges another in rut.

sanskrit: alambusas tato rājan sātyakiṃ yuddhadurmadam sasainyaṃ samare kruddho rākṣasaḥ samabhidravat
english: Then, O king, the Rākṣasa Alambusa, full of wrath, charged in battle against Sātyaki, hard to overcome in war, together with his troops.

sanskrit: bhūriśravā raṇe yatto dhṛṣṭaketum ayodhayat śrutāyuṣaṃ tu rājānaṃ dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Bhūriśravas, intent in the fight, did battle with Dhṛṣṭaketu, while Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Dharma engaged King Śrutāyus.

sanskrit: cekitānas tu samare kṛpam evānvayodhayat śeṣāḥ pratiyayur yattā bhīmam eva mahāratham
english: Cekitāna in the battle fought against Kṛpa; the rest, intent upon it, advanced against Bhīma, that mighty chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: tato rājasahasrāṇi parivavrur dhanaṃjayam śaktitomaranārācagadāparighapāṇayaḥ
english: Then kings by the thousands surrounded Dhanaṃjaya, their hands grasping spears, lances, iron arrows, maces, and bludgeons.

sanskrit: arjuno 'tha bhṛśaṃ kruddho vārṣṇeyam idam abravīt paśya mādhava sainyāni dhārtarāṣṭrasya saṃyuge vyūḍhāni vyūhaviduṣā gāṅgeyena mahātmanā
english: Then Arjuna, exceedingly wrathful, spoke thus to the descendant of Vṛṣṇi: "Behold, O Mādhava, the armies of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son drawn up for battle by the great-souled son of Gaṅgā, who knows the art of arrays.

sanskrit: yuddhābhikāmāñ śūrāṃś ca paśya mādhava daṃśitān trigartarājaṃ sahitaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ paśya keśava
english: Behold the heroes eager for battle, clad in mail, O Mādhava; behold the king of the Trigartas together with his brothers, O Keśava.

sanskrit: adyaitān pātayiṣyāmi paśyatas te janārdana ya ime māṃ yaduśreṣṭha yoddhukāmā raṇājire
english: This day I shall lay them low before your very eyes, O Janārdana — these who, O best of the Yadus, are eager to fight with me upon the field of battle."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu kaunteyo dhanurjyām avamṛjya ca vavarṣa śaravarṣāṇi narādhipagaṇān prati
english: Having spoken thus, the son of Kuntī, stroking the string of his bow, rained down showers of arrows upon the throngs of kings.

sanskrit: te 'pi taṃ parameṣvāsāḥ śaravarṣair apūrayan taḍāgam iva dhārābhir yathā prāvṛṣi toyadā
english: Those great archers in their turn filled him with showers of arrows, as the rain-clouds fill a pool with their downpour in the season of the rains.

sanskrit: hāhākāro mahān āsīt tava sainye viśāṃ pate chādyamānau bhṛśaṃ kṛṣṇau śarair dṛṣṭvā mahāraṇe
english: A great cry of woe arose within your army, O lord of peoples, when they saw the two Kṛṣṇas heavily overspread with arrows in that great battle.

sanskrit: devā devarṣayaś caiva gandharvāś ca mahoragāḥ vismayaṃ paramaṃ jagmur dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇau tathāgatau
english: The gods, the divine seers, the Gandharvas, and the great serpents were struck with the utmost wonder to behold the two Kṛṣṇas brought to such a pass.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho 'rjuno rājann aindram astram udīrayat tatrādbhutam apaśyāma vijayasya parākramam
english: Then, in his wrath, O king, Arjuna sent forth the weapon of Indra; and there we beheld the marvellous prowess of the Victor.

sanskrit: śastravṛṣṭiṃ parair muktāṃ śaraughair yad avārayat na ca tatrāpy anirbhinnaḥ kaś cid āsīd viśāṃ pate
english: For with floods of arrows he warded off the rain of weapons loosed by his foes; and yet there was not one there, O lord of peoples, who was left unpierced.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ rājasahasrāṇāṃ hayānāṃ dantināṃ tathā dvābhyāṃ tribhiḥ śaraiś cānyān pārtho vivyādha māriṣa
english: Among those thousands of kings, and their horses and elephants likewise, the son of Pṛthā pierced one with two shafts and another with three, O honored one.

sanskrit: te hanyamānāḥ pārthena bhīṣmaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ yayuḥ agādhe majjamānānāṃ bhīṣmas trātābhavat tadā
english: Being struck down by the son of Pṛthā, they fled to Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu; and for those sinking in the fathomless deep, Bhīṣma then became their savior.

sanskrit: āpatadbhis tu tais tatra prabhagnaṃ tāvakaṃ balam saṃcukṣubhe mahārāja vātair iva mahārṇavaḥ
english: As they came rushing back there in rout, your broken army was thrown into turmoil, O great king, like the mighty ocean lashed by the winds.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tathā pravṛtte saṃgrāme nivṛtte ca suśarmaṇi prabhagneṣu ca vīreṣu pāṇḍavena mahātmanā
english: Saṃjaya said: When the battle had thus broken out, and Suśarman had withdrawn, and the heroes had been routed by the great-souled Pāṇḍava,

sanskrit: kṣubhyamāṇe bale tūrṇaṃ sāgarapratime tava pratyudyāte ca gāṅgeye tvaritaṃ vijayaṃ prati
english: while your army, the like of the ocean, was being swiftly thrown into tumult, and the son of Gaṅgā had hastened forth to meet the Victor,

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā duryodhano rājan raṇe pārthasya vikramam tvaramāṇaḥ samabhyetya sarvāṃs tān abravīn nṛpān
english: King Duryodhana, beholding the prowess of the son of Pṛthā in the battle, came up in haste and spoke to all those kings,

sanskrit: teṣāṃ ca pramukhe śūraṃ suśarmāṇaṃ mahābalam madhye sarvasya sainyasya bhṛśaṃ saṃharṣayan vacaḥ
english: and at their head, in the midst of all the army, to the mighty hero Suśarman especially, with words that greatly kindled their spirit:

sanskrit: eṣa bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo yoddhukāmo dhanaṃjayam sarvātmanā kuruśreṣṭhas tyaktvā jīvitam ātmanaḥ
english: "Here is Bhīṣma, the son of Śaṃtanu, foremost of the Kurus, eager with his whole soul to fight Dhanaṃjaya, having cast away his very life.

sanskrit: taṃ prayāntaṃ parānīkaṃ sarvasainyena bhāratam saṃyattāḥ samare sarve pālayadhvaṃ pitāmaham
english: As that Bhārata advances upon the enemy's host with the whole army, do you all, intent in the battle, guard the grandsire."

sanskrit: bāḍham ity evam uktvā tu tāny anīkāni sarvaśaḥ narendrāṇāṃ mahārāja samājagmuḥ pitāmaham
english: "So be it," they said, and with that those troops of the kings, O great king, gathered together from every side about the grandsire.

sanskrit: tataḥ prayātaḥ sahasā bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo 'rjunam raṇe bhāratam āyāntam āsasāda mahābalam
english: Then Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu, advancing suddenly, fell upon the mighty Bhārata Arjuna as he came on in the battle.

sanskrit: mahāśvetāśvayuktena bhīmavānaraketunā mahatā meghanādena rathenāti virājata
english: Borne upon his great chariot — yoked with pure-white horses, bearing the standard of the dread ape, thundering like a cloud — he shone exceedingly.

sanskrit: samare sarvasainyānām upayātaṃ dhanaṃjayam abhavat tumulo nādo bhayād dṛṣṭvā kirīṭinam
english: As Dhanaṃjaya advanced in the battle, a tumultuous outcry arose from all the troops out of fear at the sight of the Diademed One.

sanskrit: abhīśuhastaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ca dṛṣṭvādityam ivāparam madhyaṃdinagataṃ saṃkhye na śekuḥ prativīkṣitum
english: And seeing Kṛṣṇa, the reins in his hands, like a second sun risen to its noonday height upon the field, they were not able to gaze upon him.

sanskrit: tathā śāṃtanavaṃ bhīṣmaṃ śvetāśvaṃ śvetakārmukam na śekuḥ pāṇḍavā draṣṭuṃ śvetagraham ivoditam
english: Even so the Pāṇḍavas were not able to look upon Bhīṣma, the son of Śaṃtanu, with his white horses and his white bow, like the white planet risen on high.

sanskrit: sa sarvataḥ parivṛtas trigartaiḥ sumahātmabhiḥ bhrātṛbhis tava putraiś ca tathānyaiś ca mahārathaiḥ
english: He was surrounded on every side by the high-souled Trigartas, by his brothers, by your sons, and by other mighty chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: bhāradvājas tu samare matsyaṃ vivyādha patriṇā dhvajaṃ cāsya śareṇājau dhanuś caikena cicchide
english: The son of Bharadvāja in the battle pierced the Matsya king with a feathered shaft, and with arrows cut down his banner and his bow, each with a single one, on the field.

sanskrit: tad apāsya dhanuś chinnaṃ virāṭo vāhinīpatiḥ anyad ādatta vegena dhanur bhārasahaṃ dṛḍham śarāṃś cāśīviṣākārāñ jvalitān pannagān iva
english: Casting aside that severed bow, Virāṭa the commander of the host swiftly took up another, firm and able to bear the strain, and arrows shaped like venomous snakes, blazing like serpents.

sanskrit: droṇaṃ tribhiḥ pravivyādha caturbhiś cāsya vājinaḥ dhvajam ekena vivyādha sārathiṃ cāsya pañcabhiḥ dhanur ekeṣuṇāvidhyat tatrākrudhyad dvijarṣabhaḥ
english: He pierced Droṇa with three shafts and his horses with four, struck his banner with one and his charioteer with five, and his bow with a single arrow; thereat the bull among the twice-born was enraged.

sanskrit: tasya droṇo 'vadhīd aśvāñ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ aṣṭābhir bharataśreṣṭha sūtam ekena patriṇā
english: Droṇa slew his horses with eight arrows with smooth-bending joints, O best of the Bharatas, and his charioteer with one feathered shaft.

sanskrit: sa hatāśvād avaplutya syandanād dhatasārathiḥ āruroha rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ śaṅkhasya rathināṃ varaḥ
english: His horses slain and his charioteer dead, that best of chariot-warriors leapt down from his car and swiftly mounted the chariot of Śaṅkha.

sanskrit: tatas tu tau pitāputrau bhāradvājaṃ rathe sthitau mahatā śaravarṣeṇa vārayām āsatur balāt
english: Then those two, father and son, standing upon the one chariot, held off the son of Bharadvāja by main force with a great shower of arrows.

sanskrit: bhāradvājas tataḥ kruddhaḥ śaram āśīviṣopamam cikṣepa samare tūrṇaṃ śaṅkhaṃ prati janeśvara
english: Then the son of Bharadvāja, in his wrath, swiftly hurled in the battle an arrow like a venomous serpent against Śaṅkha, O lord of men.

sanskrit: sa tasya hṛdayaṃ bhittvā pītvā śoṇitam āhave jagāma dharaṇiṃ bāṇo lohitārdrīkṛtacchaviḥ
english: Cleaving his heart and drinking his blood in the fray, that arrow passed on into the earth, its surface drenched and reddened with gore.

sanskrit: sa papāta rathāt tūrṇaṃ bhāradvājaśarāhataḥ dhanus tyaktvā śarāṃś caiva pitur eva samīpataḥ
english: Struck by the arrow of the son of Bharadvāja, he fell swiftly from the chariot, letting go his bow and arrows, close beside his own father.

sanskrit: hataṃ svam ātmajaṃ dṛṣṭvā virāṭaḥ prādravad bhayāt utsṛjya samare droṇaṃ vyāttānanam ivāntakam
english: Seeing his own son slain, Virāṭa fled in terror, abandoning in the battle Droṇa, who was like Death with gaping jaws.

sanskrit: bhāradvājas tatas tūrṇaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahācamūm dārayām āsa samare śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Then the son of Bharadvāja swiftly rent asunder the great host of the Pāṇḍavas in the battle, by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍy api mahārāja drauṇim āsādya saṃyuge ājaghāna bhruvor madhye nārācais tribhir āśugaiḥ
english: Śikhaṇḍin too, O great king, closing with the son of Droṇa in the encounter, struck him between the brows with three swift iron arrows.

sanskrit: sa babhau naraśārdūlo lalāṭe saṃsthitais tribhiḥ śikharaiḥ kāñcanamayair merus tribhir ivocchritaiḥ
english: With those three set upon his forehead, that tiger among men shone like Meru with three golden peaks reared aloft.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā tataḥ kruddho nimeṣārdhāc chikhaṇḍinaḥ sūtaṃ dhvajam atho rājaṃs turagān āyudhaṃ tathā śarair bahubhir uddiśya pātayām āsa saṃyuge
english: Then Aśvatthāman, enraged, in half the twinkling of an eye, O king, took aim with many arrows at Śikhaṇḍin's charioteer, his banner, his horses, and his weapon, and brought them all down in the fight.
